title: What name does each of these four angles get?
description: Four angles are placed on one line that runs from zero to one hundred eighty degrees, with marks at ninety and one hundred eighty. Each angle is named by comparing its measure with those two marks. Keeko doubts that ninety degrees is obtuse because it looks big.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the measure with ninety and one hundred eighty to name the kind of angle. Watch for students who call ninety degrees obtuse because it looks big.

source: Name each angle as acute, right, obtuse or straight: 35°, 90°, 120°, 180°.
video_script.why: The child sees that the kind of an angle comes from comparing its measure with ninety and one hundred eighty degrees.
video_script.substitution: Place each measure on a line from 0 to 180 and compare it with the marks at 90 and 180.
video_script.anchor: four angles drawn as two arms each, with a line below marked at ninety and one hundred eighty degrees
video_script.wrong_answer: ninety degrees is obtuse, because it is a big angle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says ninety degrees is obtuse because it looks big. Ninety degrees is exactly a square corner, and an obtuse angle must be wider than that.
video_script.payoff_line: Each name comes from comparing the measure with ninety and one hundred eighty

final_answer.spoken: thirty five degrees is acute, ninety is right, one hundred twenty is obtuse and one hundred eighty is straight

maths_rules: right angle = 90° (a quarter turn); straight angle = 180° (a half turn)
acute: more than 0° and less than 90°
obtuse: more than 90° and less than 180°
video_script.design: One line from 0° to 180° with marks at 90° and 180°; each angle is dropped onto the line and named. Teal for acute, amber for obtuse.

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Lay out the turns from zero to one hundred eighty degrees on one line.
<bookmark mark='right'/>A right angle is ninety degrees, a quarter turn.
<bookmark mark='acute'/>An angle smaller than ninety degrees is called acute.
<bookmark mark='obtuse'/>An angle between ninety and one hundred eighty degrees is called obtuse.
<bookmark mark='straight'/>A straight angle is one hundred eighty degrees, a half turn.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four angles of thirty five, ninety, one hundred twenty and one hundred eighty degrees.

beats.on_screen: To find: the name of each angle

marks.find: the words the name of each angle are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to name the kind of each angle.

marks.first: 35° is placed on the line before the 90° mark and labelled acute

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, compare thirty five degrees with ninety degrees.
Thirty five is less than ninety, so the angle is acute.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 90° = a quarter turn, so 90° is a right angle

marks.second: 90° sits on the square corner and is labelled right

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, compare ninety degrees with a quarter turn.
Ninety degrees is exactly a quarter turn, so it is a right angle.

marks.third: 120° is placed between the 90° and 180° marks and labelled obtuse

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step three, compare one hundred twenty degrees with both marks.
It is more than ninety and less than one hundred eighty, so it is obtuse.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 180° = a half turn, so 180° is a straight angle

marks.fourth: 180° sits on the flat line and is labelled straight

narration: <bookmark mark='fourth'/>Step four, compare one hundred eighty degrees with a half turn.
It is exactly a half turn, so it is a straight angle.

marks.pay: the words compare with 90° and 180° glow

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Each name comes from comparing the measure with ninety and one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirty five degrees is acute, and ninety is right.
One hundred twenty is obtuse, and one hundred eighty is straight.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says 90° is obtuse and is then crossed out; the square corner is laid on the 90° angle and fits exactly; the obtuse stretch begins just after the square corner

marks.square: the square corner is laid on the 90° angle and fits exactly
marks.fix: the bubble is crossed out and the obtuse stretch is shown starting after the corner

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks ninety degrees is obtuse, because it is a big angle.
<bookmark mark='square'/>But ninety degrees fits a square corner exactly.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>An obtuse angle must be wider than a square corner, so ninety degrees is a right angle.
